statement.p: Verify Stokes' Theorem for the given vector field and surface, oriented with an upward-pointing normal:
\mathbf{F} = \left\lt e^{y-z}, 0,0\right>,\quad the square with vertices (7,0,5), (7,7,5), (0,7,5), and (0,0,5).

static.solution:
Step 1. Compute the integral around the boundary curve.
The boundary consists of four segments {\mathcal{C}}_1, {\mathcal{C}}_2, {\mathcal{C}}_3, and {\mathcal{C}}_4 shown in the figure:
A=\left(0,0,5\right),\quad B=\left(0,7,5\right),\quad C=\left(7,7,5\right),\quad D=\left(7,0,5\right)
We parametrize the segments by {\mathcal{C}}_1: {\gamma }_1(t)=(t,0,5),\quad 0\le t\le 7 {\mathcal{C}}_2: {\gamma }_2(t)=(7,t,5),\quad 0\le t\le 7 {\mathcal{C}}_3: {\gamma }_3(t)=(7-t,7,5),\quad 0\le t\le 7 {\mathcal{C}}_4: {\gamma }_4(t)=(0,7-t,5),\quad 0\le t\le 7 We compute the following values: \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_1(t)\right) = \left\lt e^{y-z},0,0 \right> = \left\lt e^{-5},0,0 \right> \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_2(t)\right) = \left\lt e^{y-z},0,0 \right> = \left\lt e^{t-5},0,0 \right> \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_3(t)\right) = \left\lt e^{y-z},0,0 \right> = \left\lt e^{2},0,0 \right> \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_4(t)\right) = \left\lt e^{y-z},0,0 \right> = \left\lt e^{-t+2},0,0 \right> Hence, \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_1(t)\right)\cdot {\gamma}_1'(t) = \left\lt e^{-5},0,0 \right>\cdot \left\lt 1,0,0 \right> = e^{-5} \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_2(t)\right)\cdot {\gamma }_2'(t)= \left\lt e^{t-5},0,0 \right>\cdot \left\lt 0,1,0 \right> =0 \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_3(t)\right)\cdot {\gamma }_3'(t) = \left\lt e^{2},0,0\right>\cdot \left\lt -1,0,0 \right> =-e^{2} \mathbf{F} \left({\gamma}_4(t)\right)\cdot {\gamma }_4'(t) = \left\lt e^{-t+2},0,0 \right>\cdot \left\lt 0,-1,0 \right>=0 We obtain the following integral: \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{s}= \sum_{i=1}^4 \int_{{\mathcal{C}}_i} \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{s} =\int_0^{7} e^{-5} \,dt+0+\int_0^{7} -e^{2} \,dt+0 = 7 \left(e^{-5}-e^{2} \right) \quad \mathbf{(1)} Step 2. Compute the \text{curl}.
\text{curl} (\mathbf{F}) = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} \mathbf{i} \amp \mathbf{j} \amp \mathbf{k} \\ \frac{\partial }{\partial x}\amp \frac{\partial }{\partial y}\amp \frac{\partial }{\partial z}\\ e^{y-z}\amp 0\amp 0\end{array}\right| =-e^{y-z} \mathbf{j} - e^{y-z} \mathbf{k} = \left\lt 0,- e^{y-z},- e^{y-z} \right> Step 3. Compute the flux of the curl through the surface.
We parametrize the surface by \Phi (x,y)=(x,y,5),\quad 0\le x,\,y\le 7 The upward pointing normal is \mathbf{n} = \left\lt 0,0,1 \right>. We express \text{curl} (\mathbf{F}) in terms of the parameters x and y: \text{curl} (\mathbf{F})\left(\Phi (x,y)\right) = \left\lt 0,- e^{y-5},- e^{y-5} \right> Hence, \text{curl} (\mathbf{F})\cdot \mathbf{n} = \left\lt 0,- e^{y-5},- e^{y-5} \right>\cdot \left\lt 0,0,1 \right> =- e^{y-5} The surface integral is thus \iint_{\mathcal{S}} \text{curl} (\mathbf{F})\cdot \,d\mathbf{S} = \iint_{\mathcal{D}} - e^{y-5} \,dA=\int_0^{7} \int_0^{7} - e^{y-5} \,dy \,dx= 7\int_0^{7} - e^{y-5} \,dy=7\left(- e^{y-5}\bigg|_0^{7}\right)= 7\left(-e^{7-5}+ e^{-5}\right)=7\left(e^{-5}-e^{2}\right)\quad \mathbf{(2)} We see that the integrals in \mathbf{(1)} and \mathbf{(2)} are equal.
